newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EMU council to guide euro exchange rate - Maystadt.
newsitem.headline: EMU council to guide euro exchange rate - Maystadt.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt said on Monday a proposed "stability council" could be used to guide the external exchange rate of the single European currency, the euro.

"The second objective of such a council would be to discuss the exchange rate of the euro against the world's other currencies...it's clear the participants in monetary union should have a priviledged say in the matter," Maystadt told a news conference after meeting his French counterpart Jean Arthuis.

Maystadt said the other objectives of a stability council would be to coordinate economic policies within a euro zone and lastly to discuss the representation of EU members within international organisations such as the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

"There will be changes in the IMF because we will have to find the best way for EMU members to be represented," Maystadt, who is also chairman of the IMF's policy-making interim committee, told Reuters after the news conference.
Both Arthuis and Maystadt reiterated the informal stability council was not intended to survey or control the activities of the European Central Bank.
Maystadt noted also that ultimately it would be for all European Union finance ministers to have the final say on the external value of the euro. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
